 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086  MFA No. 101914 of 2023  THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHIVASHANKAR AMARANNAVAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the quantum and also the order of pay and recover in the judgment dated 02.01.2023 passed in MVC No.23/2012 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Yelburga.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Yelburga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Respondent No.1 filed a claim petition contending that on 07.10.2011 at about 4:00 pm when he was traveling in APE Pick-up vehicle bearing No.KA-35/A- 2126 from Itagi to Belageri village and on the way due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the said vehicle, the vehicle turned turtle on the road and as a result, he sustained severe injuries.
With that he made a claim petition seeking compensation.

3. The Tribunal after recording evidence and appreciating the evidence on record has allowed the petition directing the respondent No.2 - owner of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086 vehicle to pay the compensation and also ordered the insurance company to pay and recover the same from respondent No.2/ owner.
The said judgment and award has been challenged by the insurance company in this appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.3.
Respondent No.2 even after service of notice remained absent and unrepresented.
5.

Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the claimant is a gratuitous passenger travelling in a goods vehicle and therefore there is a fundamental breach of policy conditions, on that basis the Tribunal ought to have totally exonerated the insurance company.
He contends that the quantum awarded by the Tribunal is also on a higher side.

He contends that the Doctor has Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Basappa S/O Irappa Ulagaddi on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34318890/
2 assessed the total disability as 75% and the Tribunal has taken the disability as 100%.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Basappa S/O Irappa Ulagaddi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that Tribunal has taken the age of the claimant as 45 years NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086 based on the wound certificate but, as per the Police records his age is 50 years and as per the disability certificate his age is 55 years.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have taken the age of the injured accordingly.
He contends that considering the age of the injured, he is entitled to future prospectus of 10% as against 25% awarded by the Tribunal.
With this he prayed to allow the appeal.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 - claimant would contend that the injured has sustained paraplegia and taking into consideration that he is a coolie/agriculturist it has rightly taken the disability of whole body of 100%, even though the Doctor has assessed the disability of whole body as 75%.
He contends that the Tribunal has taken the correct age of the injured as 45 years based on the wound certificate.

He admits that the Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at Rs.6,500/-
per month and it ought to have taken the notional income of Rs.6,000/- as per the chart prepared by NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086 the legal services authority for settlement of disputes in Lok-Adalat for the year 2011, with this he prayed to dismiss the appeal.
7. Having heard the learned counsels, the Court has perused the impugned judgment and award and the other materials placed on record.
8. It is not in dispute that the injured - claimant was a gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle and there is a breach of policy condition.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has ordered for pay and recovery.

The Full Bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited,
Bijapur Vs. Yallavva and Another1, held that the insurance company is required to pay the adjudged compensation at the first instance and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Limited,
Bijapur Vs. Yallavva and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The appellant is a insurance company and respondent No.2 is a owner of the vehicle, as there is a breach of policy conditions, the Tribunal has rightly held that owner has to pay the amount 2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB) NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086 of compensation as awarded and it is first to be paid by the insurance company and insurance company can recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in question.
9.
The age of the claimant as per wound certificate is 45 years, as per Police records 50 years and as per disability certificate 55 years.
The Tribunal has taken the age of the injured as 45 years based on the wound certificate.
When there are three documents contain three different ages, it is preferable to take average of all three ages which comes to 50 years.
Therefore, the age of the injured - claimant is taken as 50 years.
Considering the age of the injured, he is entitled to future prospectus at 10% as against 25% awarded by the Tribunal.
10. The injured - claimant has sustained injury by which he has suffered paraplegia.
The Doctor has assessed the disability of the whole body at 75%.
The injured - claimant is a coolie/ agriculturist.

Considering these aspect, he has suffered paraplegia, it is impossible for the NC:
2024:KHC-D:13086 injured - claimant to continue the coolie/agriculturist.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken the disability of the whole body of injured as 100%.
The compensation awarded under the other heads are not disputed.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Basappa S/O Irappa Ulagaddi on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other heads of compensation awarded are remained undeterred.
In view of the same, the respondent No.1 is entitle to total compensation of Rs.12,65,907/- as against Rs.13,28,307/- awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The respondent No.1 - claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,65,907/-
as against Rs.13,28,307/- awarded by the NC: 2024:KHC-D:13086 Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
iii) The order of pay and recover as passed by the Tribunal remained unaltered.
iv) The appellant - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
v) Amount in deposit is ordered to be  transmitted to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
 (SHIVASHANKAR AMARANNAVAR)
